answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the juniper check immediately, the horizon audit keeps the resolved set and the atlas replay shows exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 224 aliases as a result pays the reading cost 224 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
